name: org.machanism.machai:machai-mcp-server
description: Machai MCP Server is a Java 17 server implementation for the Model Context Protocol (MCP) built on the Machai AI framework. It provides an executable server entry point and reusable Java classes for exposing GenAI tools, prompts, and resources over MCP transports. The artifact supports STDIO mode for process-based MCP integrations and HTTP remote mode through Jetty, including stateless and streamable session-capable HTTP server variants. It loads functional GenAI tools from Machai configuration using org.machanism.machai.ai provider abstractions and integrates with io.modelcontextprotocol.sdk. Typical use cases include embedding AI-powered tool execution into developer tools, coding assistants, automation agents, and applications that need MCP-compatible access to Machai FunctionTools. The library does not publish its own domain tools; it provides the server runtime and adapter infrastructure required to host additional libraries that implement functional tools and prompts.

constructors.description: Creates a stateless HTTP MCP server that reports the provided server name and version to MCP clients. Configure the port with org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.AbstractHttpMcpServer.setPort(int), load tools with org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.HttpStatelessMcpServer.tools(org.machanism.macha.core.commons.configurator.Configurator), then start it.

examples.description: Creates and starts a stateless HTTP MCP server on port 45000. Provide a real org.machanism.macha.core.commons.configurator.Configurator instance to load Machai tool libraries before starting the server.

constructors.description: Creates a streamable HTTP MCP server variant for remote MCP usage where session or streamable transport behavior is required. It supports the same project directory, port, and tool-loading configuration workflow as other HTTP MCP server implementations.

examples.description: Creates a streamable remote MCP server. Use this when clients require streamable HTTP MCP semantics rather than stateless HTTP handling.

features.name: McpServer.main
features.signature: public static void main(java.lang.String[] args) throws java.lang.Exception
features.description: Executable entry point for starting the MCP server. It parses command-line options and starts either STDIO mode by default or remote HTTP mode when a port is supplied. Supported options include -h or --help, -n or --name for server name, -d or --projectDir for working directory, -v or --version for server version, -p or --port for HTTP mode, and -s or --session for streamable HTTP server mode.

examples.description: Runs the server in default STDIO mode for local MCP clients that communicate through standard input and output.
Runs a remote stateless HTTP MCP server on port 45000.
Runs a streamable HTTP MCP server on port 45000 for clients that need session-capable streamable remote MCP behavior.

examples.title: Install as a Maven dependency for embedding an MCP server in a Java application
steps: Add the Maven dependency org.machanism.machai:machai-mcp-server:1.2.2-SNAPSHOT to your project.
Ensure Java 17 or later is used.
Set the project directory and port, load your Machai tool libraries through a configurator, and call start().
examples.snippet:
<dependency>
  <groupId>org.machanism.machai</groupId>
  <artifactId>machai-mcp-server</artifactId>
  <version>1.2.2-SNAPSHOT</version>
</dependency>

org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.HttpStatelessMcpServer server = new org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.HttpStatelessMcpServer("embedded-mcp", "1.0.0");
server.setProjectDir(new java.io.File("/workspace/project"));
server.setPort(45000);
// server.tools(configurator);
server.start();
examples.description: This scenario embeds the MCP server directly in a Java process and exposes configured Machai tools over HTTP.

examples.title: Run the ready-to-use executable server in STDIO mode
steps: Build or obtain the packaged JAR with dependencies, typically produced with the Maven pack profile.
Configure the MCP client to launch the JAR as a subprocess.
Pass --projectDir to point hosted tools at the workspace they should operate on.
Do not pass --port when STDIO mode is required.
examples.description: STDIO mode is suitable for local MCP clients that start the server process and communicate through standard input and output.

examples.title: Run the ready-to-use executable server as a remote HTTP MCP server
steps: Build or obtain the packaged JAR with dependencies.
Choose a listening port such as 45000.
Start the server with --port for stateless HTTP mode or with both --port and --session for streamable session-capable mode.
Point an MCP-compatible remote client at the HTTP endpoint exposed by the Jetty server.
examples.description: Remote HTTP mode is appropriate for integrations where MCP clients connect over the network instead of launching a local STDIO subprocess.
